answer: Because the entropy is measured at the ridge gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the wander audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 34 variations of one paragraph therefore pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the cedar panel. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, since it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
